artifacts.summary: All 8 plan phases completed: plan-level-Status ownership boundary rolled into 14 implementation agents and lint-enforced (Check G); a shared Status-line grammar library wired into validate-artifact.sh as a new error-level check; the general-research-agent.md report-heading drift fixed; a fan-out prohibition and bidirectional marker/commit-synchrony contract added to phase-closure.md; full redeploy and deployed-tree re-verification confirmed green.

completion_data.completion_summary: Closed the plan-level Status field ownership gap on both the producer side (14 implementation agent contracts now carry a lint-enforced MUST-NOT bullet forbidding hand-edits to the plan metadata Status field) and the validator side (validate-artifact.sh now rejects the three malformed Status-line shapes as errors via a new shared grammar library). Also fixed the general-research-agent.md report-heading drift, and added a fan-out prohibition plus bidirectional marker/commit-synchrony contract to phase-closure.md.

memory_candidates.content: When a predicate-sweep enumeration in a plan's Scope Hypothesis disagrees with re-sweeping at implementation time, trust the re-sweep. Example: a plan hypothesized 13 in-scope agent files for a lint-enforced contract bullet, explicitly excluding one file as 'no phase-heading write authority to bound' -- re-running the predicate at implementation time found that file DOES instruct editing phase-heading markers via the Edit tool, contradicting the plan's own claim. The fix was to trust the fresh sweep (14 files) over the stale hypothesis, and record the divergence explicitly in both the canonical fragment and the lint's in-scope array.

A test suite that resolves its script-under-test via a deploy-tree-first / source-store-fallback candidate list (the established convention for scripts under agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/) will silently test the STALE deployed copy if the source-store change has not yet been redeployed. When authoring a new suite alongside a source-store-only change, run deploy-headless.sh once early (not only at the end) so the suite's own acceptance criterion (exits 0) can be satisfied during authoring, not deferred entirely to a later redeploy phase.

The full verify-deploy.sh gate set (not just deploy-headless.sh's fast subset) can surface real defects introduced by a task's own new files that neither the task's own new test suite nor the fast gates catch -- e.g. a new context/contracts/*.md fragment file with no corresponding entry in the extension's index-entries.json (caught by check-extension-docs.sh's Rule S, doc-lint gate). Always run the full gate set at least once before declaring a task's redeploy phase done, not only the fast/default subset.
